scenario.label: What we tell the board about next year
scenario.brief: Board meeting in three weeks. Before we build the deck I want the exec team's honest separate accounts of what next year actually looks like, because the deck always ends up being the most optimistic version in the room.
scenario.theDecision: The revenue plan assumes a market entry that the person responsible for it says is twelve months away, not four. The CEO has already told two board members the four-month version. A right answer puts the gap between the plan and the owner's own estimate in front of the CEO before the deck is written.

people.name: Victor Almeida
people.truth: The plan shows Kenya revenue from Q2. He has told two board members in one-to-ones that Kenya opens in Q2. He has not checked the date with the person doing it since June.
people.manner: Confident, persuasive, will engage seriously with a number that contradicts him.

people.name: Wanjiru Kariuki
people.remit: Head of expansion. Owns the Kenya entry.
people.truth: Licensing alone is nine to eleven months and she has the regulator's written timeline. Q2 is not possible; Q4 at the earliest, more likely the following Q1. She told the COO in June and assumed it was passed on.
people.manner: Exact. Quotes the regulator's letter and the date she sent it.

people.name: Dele Ogunbiyi
people.truth: He built the plan on the Q2 date the CEO gave him. He has never spoken to Wanjiru about it. 40% of next year's revenue line depends on it.
people.manner: Careful, numerical, uncomfortable when the assumption is questioned.

myRows.text: The single most important strategic priority is securing the operating license for Kenya.
My role is to manage the entire licensing process. I'm responsible for all the submissions, communications, and negotiations with the regulator to secure that license.
The biggest single risk is the regulator's timeline itself. "Licensing alone is nine to eleven months," according to their written timeline I received on June 10th.
I informed the COO in June that based on the regulator's written timeline, Q2 for next year is not possible for launch. Q4 at the earliest, and it's more likely to be the following Q1.
The license would be secured when we receive the official, written operating license from the regulator.
For it to be counted as delivered for next year, it would need to exist by the end of Q4 at the absolute earliest, but more realistically, by the end of Q1 the year after next.
The board might not be aligned on the realistic timeline for market entry. The deck often presents the most optimistic view, but the regulator's timeline doesn't support a quick launch.
I cannot provide a forecast for headcount right now. We haven't even received the license yet, so any numbers would be pure speculation.
